title: Validation of the PRI-MUS-TZ score and effect of online micro-ultrasound training on transitional zone prostate cancer detection
summary:
Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men. A particularly high-resolution ultrasound examination, called micro-ultrasound, can detect tumours in the prostate. However, tumours in the inner and front part of the prostate are difficult to detect because benign enlargement is common in this area. A new rating scheme has been developed for this area.
In this study, we test whether this rating scheme works reliably and whether a two-day online training helps doctors detect tumours in this area more accurately. Participants assess ultrasound recordings of patients whose diagnosis has been confirmed by tissue examination or magnetic resonance imaging, before and after the training. We then compare how well tumours are detected before and after the training.

interventions.name:
Prospective recruitment of at least 20 physicians via registration for the two-day online course "Mannheim Micro-Ultrasound Curriculum" focusing on the transition zone; enrolment after written informed consent.
Before training, all participants receive written material on the definitions of the PRI

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Physicians registered for the online course of the Mannheim Micro-Ultrasound Curriculum; consent to study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Involvement in the development of the PRI-MUS-TZ score, the selection of test cases or the conduct of the study
